text:
maria: Heads up — proposal for an auto-fallback "thermostat" we talked about. Idea: instead of binary fallback we expose a risk-gated degradation level that scales aggressiveness based on short-term error/latency risk.

kevin: +1 for avoiding flip-flop. Can you sketch how we compute the risk score?

maria: Rough sketch: risk = weighted(5m-error-rate, 1m-latency-p50-above-slo, current-cpu-util). weights pluggable per-route. If risk>threshold we start gentle degrade (quantize+cache) then escalate.

anne: Important: need explicit audit trail for each escalation step. We can't have silent rollouts. Audit must include trigger metrics + policy id + model variant used.

sam: Agree. Also want a UI timeline in Console: show when thermostat changed setpoint, with links to traces and the exact policy JSON.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch feature/autofallback-thermostat by @maria — test cluster target: canary-3 — ETA 02:00 UTC.

maria: Here's a minimal policy prototype (json) — this is what the console would save:

```json
{"policy_id": "thermo-v1", "route": "/v1/generate", "risk_weights": {"errors": 0.6, "latency": 0.3, "cpu": 0.1}, "levels": [{"name":"gentle","actions":[{"type":"cache_prefix","ttl_s":30},{"type":"quantize","bits":8}]},{"name":"aggressive","actions":[{"type":"batch","max_tokens":256},{"type":"fallback_variant","model":"redwood-small-quant"}]}], "audit": {"enabled": true, "retention_days":90}}
```

kevin: Nice. Two questions: 1) how do we avoid oscillation when risk hovers around threshold? 2) who can modify risk_weights?

maria: 1) hysteresis + cool-down window (default 3m) and require monotonic step escalation. 2) console RBAC: only owners and platform-admin role can edit. We also keep immutable history so changes append a new policy-version.

anne: For telemetry, we need per-decision telemetry events: `fallback.decision` with fields: policy_id, level, trigger_value, metrics_snapshot, actor (auto/manual). Those events must be queryable in the Logs UI and linkable to the Trace.

sam: How about exposing simulated dry-run in the Console? Run past 24h traffic against new policy and show a predicted cost and error delta.

julie: That would be huge for SRE reviews. But simulation must be cheap. Maybe sample 1% of requests or replay trimmed traces.

maria: Implementation notes: runtime will evaluate policy in the router; decisions are synchronous but outcome write to async audit stream (kafka -> obs pipeline). Need low-latency path <150us added per-request.

kevin: Also check quota interactions: fallback actions that reduce tokens (quantize/variant) should not double-count against per-customer quota. We need to record effective_token_count in telemetry.

anne: UI: in rollout workflow, show risk threshold slider, cool-down toggle, simulated impact (cost change %, latency change ms), and a mandatory runbook field for `aggressive` level.

sam: UX nit: call it "Setpoint" in Console to give PMs a familiar metaphor. Add a one-click override to force manual `aggressive` for incidents.

maria: Good call. Next steps: I'll push the canary, include telemetry event schema, and open a short RFC for the Console components. Asking @kevin @anne for reviews on the schema before EOD. :thumbsup:

kevin: Will review. Quick thought — add `reason_code` enum to audit events so ops can filter for `latency_spike`, `model_error_spike`, `cpu_pressure`.

julie: If we go live, ops wants a retention export to S3 for compliance. Add export toggle.

maria: noted. Thanks all — ping me in thread with any hard blockers.
